reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read all six scenes, vocabulary, pause question, discussion questions, alt texts, content note, provenance and adaptation changes against Ryder's rendered text, and re-read and approved the corrected text.

Blockers fixed before approval: the frame now correctly has Victor telling the tale to Lively; false 'added' claims in the change notes were removed; the ocean taking the eggs to test the husband's boast, his second boast, the wife's call for help, and Garuda going to Vishnu, who comes to him, were restored from the source.
The pause question now comes before its answer: whether small birds together can beat the great sea.
Birds narrated in the neuter; no em dashes; Vishnu appears only in the text and is never drawn; content note truthful: the eggs are returned unharmed.
2026-10-05: the coordinator changed only the age label from 8–12 to 8+ under the new age bands (2+, 8+, 10+, 12+, 16+); no story text changed, so the text approval above still applies.
illustrations: Six equal 512px panels; seams measured exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024 on the published WebP; 1024x1536, under 650 KB; no gutters, dividing lines, bleed or vignettes; no text in any panel.
Final sheet is a composite of one generation and two edit passes; the panel 6 edit showing the four eggs is aligned exactly to the grid with no visible seam.

The lapwing pair (black head and breast, white cheeks, red wattle, yellow legs, male slightly larger) is consistent in panels 1, 2, 4 and 6; exactly four speckled olive eggs in panels 1 and 6, and an empty scrape in panel 2.
Panel 3: the lapwing leads crows, a myna, a parrot, an egret, a kingfisher and sparrows carrying clods of earth over rough sea. Panel 4: the birds gather before an old white goose.
Panel 5: Garuda is a golden-bronze eagle-like bird with no human features, flying over a sea drawn back from the sand; Vishnu, the bow and the fire arrow are not drawn.

No bird is injured and no egg broken. Accepted minor issues: the boast reads as firm resolve with a closed beak, Garuda's talons are prominent but not threatening, and the 'gander' reads as a domestic goose.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age suitability has not been tested with children.
Source fidelity was checked against the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels; not every scene was checked in the app in dark mode.
